subject: [URGENT] Pegasus - elevated 5xx/429 and timeouts affecting inference (initial report)
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pegasus.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>; Maya Chen <maya.chen@pegasus.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: High error rate and timeouts affecting inference requests

Hi Kimberly / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden rise in 5xx and 429 responses across our production inference traffic starting around 08:45 PT. Client-side SDKs are reporting timeouts and immediate retry storms — one of our services (recommendation pipeline) is backlogged and latency is spiking to >5s for many requests.

Attached is a short sample of failing request payloads and the server-side error snippets (pegasus_error_sample.log). This is impacting a portion of our customers — can you confirm receipt and an ETA for a mitigation? We're happy to accept temporary throttling/fallback recommendations.

Severity: P1 for us right now.

Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, Pegasus Systems

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up, and sorry you're seeing this.

We're opening an incident now (INC-20261130-PEG) and triaging immediately. I've looped in Dev (serving runtime) and Rishi (platform reliability). Short answers up front: we'll provide a public status page update within 30m, and a mitigation ETA in the next 45m.

- If possible, hold any planned traffic ramp for the next 2 hrs.

I'll coordinate mitigations and keep you posted every 30–60 minutes until stable.

Subject: Re: High error rate and timeouts affecting inference requests — initial triage

Quick triage notes (initial, investigating):
- Observed: sudden increase in 429 rate across the US-hosted pool serving Pegasus model variants starting 08:42 PT. 5xx (upstream model execution failures) also increased concurrently.
- Signal: queue depth for the model shards increased ~5x; KV cache thrash observed on longer-context flows.
- Hypothesis: a combination of an upstream traffic burst and aggressive client retries created transient overload on a subset of workers; some kernel timeouts surfaced as 5xx.

Short-term mitigations to apply (can be executed in next 15–30m):
1) Apply circuit-breaker policy for Pegasus routes: limit concurrent requests per-session and return 429 with Retry-After when overloaded. See runbook: runbook_circuit_breaker_v2.pdf
2) Shorten default token-timeout to reduce worker lockups for long-running requests.
3) Scale up the dedicated pool by +20% capacity and shift non-critical background jobs off that pool.
4) Recommend Pegasus reduce client retry_count to 1 and add jitter. We can return a 429 with Retry-After header to help clients back off.

I'll start the circuit-breaker changes and request autoscale now. Marissa — can you prepare a short customer status update once we have the first mitigation in place?

Dev
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Redwood status & next steps — Pegasus incident INC-20261130-PEG

Alex,

Quick status update — thank you for reporting.

What we've done so far (10:05 PT):
- Enabled a per-route circuit breaker for Pegasus traffic (will return 429 + Retry-After when overloaded).
- Triggered autoscale to add capacity to the dedicated pool serving your tenant (+20% target).
- Shortened request execution timeout on affected workers to limit long-running locks.

Expected customer-facing impact: you should see a reduction in sustained 5xx and fewer prolonged timeouts within ~15–30 minutes; short-term 429 counts may rise as the circuit breaker returns controlled backpressure (this is intended to prevent retry amplification).

Next updates:
- 10:35 PT: we will post a public incident note on https://status.redwood.com and include actionable guidance for SDK config.
- 11:30 PT: deeper post-mortem on root cause and permanent mitigations.

Attachments included: incident_timeline.xlsx (internal timeline draft), and a brief SDK guidance snippet.

We appreciate your patience. If you see anything worsening, please attach logs and a sample request and we will escalate.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Ops, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the transparency and the ETA. We'll keep you posted if we see regression.

Alex

Subject: Incident summary & next steps — Pegasus (INC-20261130-PEG)

Alex — short summary and next steps now that we're in recovery mode.

What changed:
- Circuit breaker and autoscale reduced sustained 5xx and long timeouts; overall latency for most traffic is back to normal baseline.
- We still see elevated 429 counts for very large batched requests; this is expected while client retries and legacy services converge to new backoff configs.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Redwood: implement a permanent per-tenant adaptive concurrency control (Dev / 2w).
- Redwood: add more aggressive KV cache eviction for long-context flows (Rishi / 1w).
- Pegasus: roll SDK backoff patch to all legacy services (Alex / 3d).

We will prepare a formal post-mortem (internal) and a customer-facing RCA within 5 business days. As this had customer impact, I'm looping in Sean for executive-level follow up on credits and a short CSM-led review.

We will also keep the status page updated until metrics are stable. Thank you and apologies again for the disruption — we know this is critical for your product.

Best,
